ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has five solid figures labeled A, B, C, D, E, and each figure is composed of 4 small cubes of the same size. A is 4 cubes arranged in a straight line; B is a compact 2×2 block; C is a corner/offset shape; D is a front-back offset shape; E is a T-shaped stack with 3 in a row at the bottom and 1 more placed above the middle. Reasoning: How much color is needed depends on the number of exposed cube faces. 4 separate cubes have 4×6=24 faces in total. Each time there is a pair of cube faces touching face to face, 2 faces are hidden, so the number of exposed faces = 24 - 2×number of contact pairs. A has 3 pairs of contacts, exposed faces 18; B's compact 2×2 block has 4 pairs of contacts, exposed faces 16; C, D, E all have only 3 pairs of contacts, so the exposed faces are all 18. Therefore B has the fewest exposed faces and needs the least color.

raw_record.question_text: Each figure is made up of 4 equally big cubes and coloured in. Which labeled figure needs the least amount of colour?

method.method_draft: Count exposed cube faces directly using the surface-area formula. From the image, identify the four-cube arrangement for each labeled figure: A is a straight row of 4 cubes, B is a compact 2-by-2 block, C is an L/offset arrangement, D is a staggered arrangement, and E is a T-like stack with one cube on top of the middle of a row of 3. From the text, use that all figures have exactly 4 equally sized cubes and the amount of colour depends on the number of outside faces. Start with 4 cubes having 4 × 6 = 24 faces total. For each face-to-face contact between two cubes, subtract 2 hidden faces. Count contacts in each figure: B has the most shared faces because the 2-by-2 block has 4 contacts, while the less compact figures have only 3 contacts. Therefore B has the fewest exposed faces and needs the least colour.
